skill.name: ci-pipeline-setup
skill.description: Set up GitHub Actions CI/CD workflows for Node and web projects, including linting, testing, builds, security checks, branch protection, and deployment patterns.
skill.summary: Create GitHub Actions CI/CD workflows with quality gates, branch protection, and deployment examples.
skill.author: Doyajin174

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown syntax, not executable Ruby backticks. The GitHub documentation links and GITHUB_TOKEN example are benign workflow references. One contextual risk remains: the Vercel deployment template passes secrets to a mutable third-party action.

remediation.issue: Third-party deployment action receives Vercel secrets.
remediation.suggestion: Pin the action to a reviewed commit SHA or use the official Vercel CLI, and scope tokens to deployment only.
Add least-privilege permissions to each workflow, with read-only defaults and write scopes only for required jobs.
State that agents should reference secret names only and never request, print, or hardcode secret values.

semantic_findings.title: Deployment Secrets Passed to Third-Party Action
semantic_findings.description: The Vercel deployment examples use amondnet/vercel-action@v25 with Vercel secret values. This is legitimate automation, but the third-party action can access deployment credentials.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The YAML directly pairs a non-GitHub deployment action with Vercel secret names. It is a common deployment pattern, so the issue is supply-chain exposure rather than clear malicious intent.

content.value_statement: Manual checks slow reviews and let inconsistent releases reach production. This skill creates GitHub Actions workflows with required quality gates and deployment patterns.
actual_capabilities: Drafts GitHub Actions CI workflows for lint, format, type check, tests, build, and npm audit.
Suggests package scripts for Node, TypeScript, Vitest, ESLint, Prettier, and Next.js projects.
Documents branch protection rules tied to required CI status checks.
Adds matrix testing, dependency caching, PR labeling, and Dependabot examples.
Provides Vercel production and pull request preview deployment patterns.
limitations: Targets GitHub Actions and JavaScript projects; other CI providers need adaptation.
Requires repository administrators to configure branch protection manually.
Requires users to create and scope deployment secrets before CD workflows can run.
Does not validate generated workflows against every project structure.

use_cases.title: Create a new CI baseline
use_cases.description: Add required lint, type check, test, build, and audit jobs to a new repository.

use_cases.title: Standardize pull request checks
use_cases.description: Map GitHub branch protection settings to the workflow jobs that must pass before merge.

use_cases.title: Add deployment automation
use_cases.description: Plan production and preview deployments after quality checks pass in GitHub Actions.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic CI workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new JavaScript repository.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a GitHub Actions CI workflow for this project. Include lint, type check, test, build, and npm audit jobs.

prompt_templates.title: Add branch protection guidance
prompt_templates.scenario: Connect workflow jobs to merge requirements.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the CI workflow and list the branch protection checks that should be required before pull requests can merge.

prompt_templates.title: Improve pipeline performance
prompt_templates.scenario: Optimize an existing workflow without changing release behavior.
prompt_templates.prompt: Improve this GitHub Actions pipeline with matrix testing, dependency caching, and clear job dependencies. Keep the same validation stages.

prompt_templates.title: Design full CI/CD automation
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced setup with deployment, previews, and security gates.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a full CI/CD plan for this repository. Include GitHub Actions checks, Dependabot, branch protection, Vercel deployment, required secrets, and security hardening.

output_examples.input: Create CI for a Node project with tests and TypeScript.
output: A staged GitHub Actions plan covering linting, formatting, type checks, tests, builds, and dependency audit.
Suggested package scripts that match the workflow jobs.
A merge checklist for required status checks.
A deployment plan that runs only after CI passes.
Separate production and preview deployment flows.
A list of required secret names and permission boundaries.

output_examples.input: Harden pull request validation for an existing repository.
output: Recommended branch protection settings for main branches.
Dependabot and PR labeling automation guidance.
Security notes for token handling and workflow permissions.

best_practices: Pin third-party actions to reviewed versions or commit SHAs when secrets are available.
Use GitHub Secrets and least-privilege workflow permissions for every deployment token.
Make branch protection require the same job names used in workflows.
anti_patterns: Do not bypass CI by merging directly to protected branches.
Do not store deployment tokens or API keys in workflow files.
Do not add deploy jobs before tests and builds block unsafe releases.

faq.question: Does this skill create workflow files?
faq.answer: It can help draft or edit workflow files when the agent has file access.

faq.question: Which projects fit best?
faq.answer: It fits GitHub-hosted Node, TypeScript, Next.js, and Vercel projects best.

faq.question: Can it configure branch protection automatically?
faq.answer: It explains required settings, but repository administrators must apply or automate them.

faq.question: Does it support deployment?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes production and preview deployment patterns for Vercel.

faq.question: What secrets are needed?
faq.answer: Deployment examples need GitHub Secrets such as Vercel token, organization ID, and project ID.

faq.question: Is it safe for private repositories?
faq.answer: Review third-party actions, restrict permissions, and scope tokens before enabling deployment workflows.
